Q1: The failing test in shard 1 of `orchestrate-poll (2)` (run 37883807697) is unknown. What should this issue deliver?
Choices:
A. Make shard failures name themselves. In the "Orchestrate poll process unit tests" step of `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, after a shard fails, re-emit each `  FAIL  <name>: …` line from that shard's log as its own `::error::` line next to the existing `orchestrate-poll shard N failed` error. Then annotations and the log tail name the failing test. Add a contract test (e.g. `tests/test_ci_poll_test_sharding.py`). No poller or test fix is guessed. (RECOMMENDED)
B. Reproduce locally. The implementer runs the `orchestrate-poll` group 2, shard 1 subset (same `NR % total == n` split) and fixes only a failure it actually reproduces. If everything passes, the issue closes with no change because the failure was transient.
C. Treat it as transient. Close the issue with no code change and re-run CI on PR #6858.
D. Combine A and B: add the failure-surfacing change and try to reproduce and fix the failure in the same PR.
**Note:** A and D edit `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. That is an automation path, so implement needs `ALLOW_WORKFLOW_EDITS=true` and an exact `files_touched` grant on an issue from a trusted author. If this triage-filed issue doesn't qualify, the commit will be scope-blocked. Choose B or C to avoid touching `.github/`.
